Bug_Details: Duration.get() only works with SECONDS or NANOS. Duration.get(TemporalUnit) only works when passed ChronoUnit.SECONDS or ChronoUnit.NANOS. All other values are guaranteed to throw a UnsupportedTemporalTypeException. In general, you should avoid duration.get(ChronoUnit). Instead, please use duration.toNanos(), Durations.toMicros(duration), duration.toMillis(), duration.getSeconds(), duration.toMinutes(), duration.toHours(), or duration.toDays().
Bug_Explanation: The bug is caused by trying to use Duration.get() with a temporal unit other than SECONDS or NANOS. In this code, the bug is embedded on line 6 where ChronoUnit.MINUTES is passed to duration.get().
Trigger_Explanation: The bug is triggered in the test method 'testShowBug' on line 10, where the'showBug' method from the 'DurationGetTemporalUnitBug' class is called with a duration of 120 seconds. This call triggers the bug in the'showBug' method, which attempts to use Duration.get(ChronoUnit.MINUTES) on the duration, causing an UnsupportedTemporalTypeException to be thrown.
